deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Take three pseudolines D_i (i in a 3-element index set I) in general position in the projective plane. They form the minimal arrangement. Its cell map C has 3 vertices (the pairwise intersections), 6 edges and 4 triangular faces. This is the hemi-octahedron, the quotient of the octahedron by the antipodal map; the check 3-6+4=1 = chi(RP^2) holds. The margin note 'octaèdre' refers to the octahedron, the orientation double cover on S^2.

Notation. Vertices are labelled by I: vertex i is the unique vertex not on D_i. So D_i is a bigon (2-cycle) with vertex set S_i = I\{i} and a 2-element edge set A_i.

Formalism. Grothendieck computes with 2-element sets, i.e. Z/2-torsors. The product X∧Y is the contracted product (X×Y)/(Z/2). The unit is 1, and X∧X ≃ 1 canonically. or(I) is the 2-element set of orientations (cyclic orders) of I.

Previous page. The orientation set of the bigon D_i is Omega_i ≃ S_i ∧ A_i: a vertex and an edge determine a direction, and swapping both gives the same direction. He gets ∧_i A_i ≃ 1 (10). A trivialisation of type (10) is equivalent to an isomorphism ∧_i Omega_i ≃ or(I) (11bis), i.e. (∧Omega_i)∧or(I) ≃ 1 (12).

This page.
(i) The family (Omega_i) with that datum is reinterpreted as 'a circle and an orientation of that circle'. The sentence is garbled and not justified.
(ii) Define L_i = Omega_i ∧ ∧_{α≠i}(I\{α}). The two descriptions (13) determine each other trivially, since Y∧Y ≃ 1.
(iii) Taking the product over i gives (14): ∧Omega_i ≃ ∧L_i. Each I\{α} occurs exactly twice in ∧_i ∧_{α≠i}(I\{α}), so that factor is ≃ 1. Hence also (∧Omega_i)∧or I ≃ (∧L_i)∧or I.
(iv) This last 2-element set is interpreted as the set of orientations of the combinatorial octahedron built from (Omega_i), resp. (L_i). That octahedron is the orientation double cover of the projective map.
(v) Margin: A_i is recovered as L_i ∧ ∧_{α∈I}(I\{α}) ≃ L_i ∧ or(I). This uses the canonical isomorphism ∧_{α∈I}(I\{α}) ≃ or(I): a cyclic order orders each complementary pair, and reversing it flips all three factors.

The page then opens a summarising 'Proposition' about this map C and its associated 1-complex K, continued on the next page.

Purpose. Set up a canonical, choice-free bookkeeping of orientations (lines, vertices, edges, global orientation of the double cover) for pseudoline arrangements. This is the base case of three pseudolines, presumably for a sign/orientation calculus on general arrangements.
errors: The interpretive sentence 'La famille des trois ensembles Omega_i ... définit un cercle et une orientation de ce cercle' is not justified on the page. The construction of the circle is left implicit, so it is a gap rather than an error.

In (13) the index ranges must be α∈I\{i} in both lines (consistent with the next page). The margin formula uses α∈I and should read A_i ≃ L_i ∧ ∧_{α∈I}(I\{α}) ≃ L_i ∧ or(I). With that reading it is correct.
(13) is tautological given Y∧Y≃1, and (14) follows because each I\{α} appears twice. No mathematical error, but the 'mutual determination' carries no content beyond this.

ideas.what: Calculus of 2-element sets (Z/2-torsors) under contracted product ∧ to track orientations canonically, with no choices
ideas.modern_name: Z/2-torsors / orientation torsors, determinant-line style sign bookkeeping
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (torsor formalism: Grothendieck/Giraud; orientation torsors folklore)
ideas.where_published: torsor language pervasive in SGA/Giraud; this specific sign calculus not known in print

ideas.what: Minimal arrangement of 3 pseudolines in RP^2 as a combinatorial map with 3 vertices, 6 edges, 4 triangles; its orientation double cover is the octahedron
ideas.modern_name: hemi-octahedron; simple arrangement of 3 pseudolines; orientation double cover
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Levi 1926 pseudolines; Grünbaum, Arrangements and Spreads 1972)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses cartes/dessins; pseudoline arrangements possibly alluded to, unsure

ideas.what: Canonical isomorphism ∧_{α∈I}(I\{α}) ≃ or(I) for a 3-element set, and the orientation set of the double cover expressed as (∧Omega_i)∧or(I)
ideas.modern_name: orientation of a 3-set via complementary pairs; chirotope-like sign of a basis triple
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; cf. chirotope axioms of oriented matroids (Bland–Las Vergnas, Folkman–Lawrence 1978)

missed.claim: Orientations of the pseudolines of an arrangement, and the global orientation of its double cover, are encoded as a canonical torsor identity. This is a basis-free relative of the chirotope sign data of rank-3 oriented matroids, which Grothendieck does not name. On this page it is only the trivial 3-line case.
missed.quote: (∧ Ω_i) ∧ or I ≃ (∧ L_i) ∧ or I — orientations de l'oct. comb. défini par (Ω_i)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal. It is a choice-free formulation of orientation data for pseudoline arrangements, but it is elementary and implicit in oriented matroid theory.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine sign/torsor bookkeeping for the simplest arrangement of three pseudolines (hemi-octahedron). It is correct but elementary and has no content beyond what oriented matroid / arrangement theory already handles. Only the stylistic choice of a canonical Z/2-torsor calculus is characteristically Grothendieckian.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 reads 'La famille (Ω_i)_{i∈I} des trois ensembles Ω_i : deux étant ...'. The word after the colon may be 'deux à deux'/'dans' rather than 'deux étant'; it is uncertain.
'qui donnent des isom[?] canoniques' should be 'qui donnent des isom^s canoniques' (plural abbreviation).

In the left label of (14) the underbrace text reads 'orientations de l'oct. comb. défini par (Ω_i)_{i∈I}', with 'oct' corrected from a crossed-out word; 'octa' in the transcription is not what is written.
The bottom-left margin note is probably 'octaèdre gauche' (possibly 'octaèdre' + 'grandes'). It is an annotation next to the Proposition about the 3-vertex, 6-edge, 4-face map.
Margin at (13) reads roughly: '! transport Ω_i, L_i, A_i puisque A_i ≃ ... ∧(I\{i}) ≃ L_i ∧ ∧_{α∈I}(I−α) ≃ L_i ∧ or(I) cf (9)'.
Under 'Proposition', 'qui correspondent à une paire des triangles' is more likely 'qui sont des triangles'/'correspondant à ... des triangles'; it is uncertain.
